plan.topic: Tirzepatide vs semaglutide in type 2 diabetes: the SURPASS-2 randomized head-to-head (NEJM 2021, adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, 40 weeks)
plan.angle:
13:00 lead, two-drug head-to-head with tirzepatide named first. It uses a different trial from previous Shorts (SURMOUNT-5 has already been used).

Answer by 10 s: in about 1,879 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, A1C fell more on all 3 tirzepatide doses than on semaglutide 1 mg at 40 weeks. Give per-arm A1C (with mmol/mol) and weight change, copied exactly from NEJM, with per-arm n and the estimand.

Key honesty line: the semaglutide dose was 1 mg, lower than the 2.4 mg weight-loss dose, and this was open-label. It's a different population from SURMOUNT-5. GI side effects for each drug, using per-arm figures from the paper.

'Bigger average isn't best for everyone; don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own.' 'Not personal advice' plus the full prescriber line, then 'follow for more'. 170 words or fewer. Captions keep numbers whole and match the stat pills exactly.

package.title: Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide for Type 2 Diabetes #shorts
package.description:
In the SURPASS-2 randomized head-to-head (1,879 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, 40 weeks), tirzepatide (5/10/15 mg) lowered A1C more than semaglutide 1 mg, its top diabetes dose at the time. Open-label trial. Nausea: 17-22% on tirzepatide vs 18% on semaglutide. Diarrhea: 13-16% vs 12%.

Not personal advice. Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Source: NEJM 2021;385:503-515, https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2107519

social.instagram_caption:
"Which one lowers A1C more?" is a fair question if you're living with type 2 diabetes and weighing options with your doctor.

One randomized head-to-head tested it: SURPASS-2 (NEJM, 2021).

• 1,879 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, about 470 per group, 40 weeks
• Tirzepatide 5, 10 and 15 mg: A1C fell 2.01, 2.24 and 2.30 percentage points
• Semaglutide 1 mg (its top diabetes dose at the time, not the 2.4 mg weight-loss dose): A1C fell 1.86 points
• Weight: tirzepatide down 7.6-11.2 kg across doses vs 5.7 kg on semaglutide
• Side effects: nausea 17-22% (tirzepatide) vs 18% (semaglutide); diarrhea 13-16% vs 12%

The catch: open-label, and semaglutide wasn't tested at its higher weight-loss dose here. A bigger average result doesn't mean it's the better choice for every person.

Save this for your next doctor's appointment.

#Tirzepatide #Semaglutide #Type2Diabetes #GLP1 #SURPASS2 #DiabetesManagement #A1C #MetabolicHealth

Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own. Not personal advice: talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary: I checked every number against the SURPASS-2 paper (Frías et al., NEJM 2021;385:503-515), and they're all correct. 1,879 adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin were randomized in an open-label trial lasting 40 weeks, with about 470 people in each group. On the treatment-regimen estimand, A1C fell by 2.01, 2.24 and 2.30 percentage points on tirzepatide versus 1.86 on semaglutide 1 mg. These are correctly kept apart from the efficacy-estimand figures (2.09, 2.37 and 2.46). Weight fell by 7.6, 9.3 and 11.2 kg versus 5.7 kg. Stomach side effects were nausea 17–22% vs 18%, diarrhea 13–16% vs 12% and vomiting 6–10% vs 8%. Tirzepatide's A1C advantage was statistically superior at all three doses. The mmol/mol conversions are approximately right. The caveats in "the catch" are accurate: STEP 1 used 2.4 mg, SURPASS-2 was open-label, and SURMOUNT-5 left out people with diabetes. The script cites a real randomized head-to-head trial, uses the correct population, gives side effects for both drugs, and includes the 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own' line, the disclaimer and the prescriber line. The CTA correctly falls back to 'follow for more' and names no unconfirmed video. Only small wording fixes remain.

issues.claim: Weight fell seven point six, nine point three and eleven point two kilos, versus five point seven.
issues.problem: Spoken without any drug, dose or comparator, so audio-only viewers can't tell which number belongs to which arm. Our rules say every spoken number names its arm and comparator.
issues.fix: Weight fell seven point six, nine point three and eleven point two kilos on the three tirzepatide doses, versus five point seven on semaglutide one milligram.

issues.claim: A1C fell two point zero one, two point two four and two point three points, versus one point eight six

issues.fix: Treatment-regimen estimand: on tirzepatide five, ten and fifteen milligrams, A1C fell two point zero one, two point two four and two point three zero percentage points, versus one point eight six on semaglutide one milligram.

issues.problem: Accurate, but viewers may not know that 1 mg was the top semaglutide diabetes dose when the trial ran. A higher 2 mg diabetes dose was approved later. Adding that context keeps the comparison fair to both drugs.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits at the right level already (-13.5 dB under speech, within the -12/-15 window); the only issue was pauses running hot (-11 vs ~-14 target), so I trimmed the overall bed ~1.4 dB (0.85x) rather than touching the duck. SFX levels during speech were already well inside -14/-20 dB, so the main fix was density: several transition/stat beats had 5-8 overlapping stock cues (duplicate simultaneous swooshes, ticks doubling pops) inside well under a second; I muted the redundant layers so no moment exceeds 3-4 audible effects, keeping one clean transition sound plus one or two accent hits per beat. Added a small suspense dip for "here's the catch" and a soft resolving chime on the closing disclaimer to give those two beats a little extra felt shape without raising levels.
